_note: The model-to-circuit signal correspondence, checked from both ends.
Every key names a field of a Lean model structure; every value names the circom
signal that field mirrors. `lean/scripts/check-names.py` checks the keys resolve
as Lean declarations; `test/formal/signal_parity.test.ts` checks the values exist
in the compiled `.sym`. Neither side can drift without one of them failing.
`{i<N_IN}` expands over the shape: the signal must exist at every index below the
bound, and must NOT exist at the bound itself. That pins the arity as well as the
name, so `Transact(11, 4, 6)` is checked against the circuit rather than asserted
`absent` is not a list of gaps. Each entry is a signal the optimizer removed
because a constraint pins it to a constant or merges it with another wire, and
the reason is the interesting part: `all_dummy.out` is gone because
`all_dummy.out === 0` holds it at zero, which is the constraint
`TransactSat.not_all_dummy` models. If one of these reappears, that constraint
A field can be in both sections when the signal array survives except at one
end: `vbLhs` is present from index 1 and absent at index 0, `vbRhs` present below
its top and absent at it, `dgBlock` present for every block but the last,
whose output is the public `digest` signal.

TxWitness.dummyAllOut.why: `all_dummy.out === 0` (transact.circom:107) pins it, so the optimizer folds it to the constant. That constraint is `TransactSat.not_all_dummy`, and `TxWellFormed.someRealInput` is what it buys; if this signal comes back, the constraint is gone.

TxWitness.zIsZero.why: `z_nz.out === 0` (poly_eval.circom:37) pins it. That constraint is `PolyEvalSat.z_nonzero`, and `TxWellFormed.challengeNonzero` is what it buys; if this signal comes back, the challenge may be zero, and at `z = 0` only the first coefficient reaches `y`.

OutputSlot.assetIsZero.why: `asset_nz.out === 0` (output.circom:33) is unconditional on an output, unlike `SpentNote`'s `(1 - is_dummy) * asset_nz.out === 0`, which is why the spent counterpart survives and this does not. Asset id 0 means "no asset".

TxWitness.dummyAcc.why: `dummy_acc[0] <== 0` is the chain's base, folded to a constant. Later entries survive; the model's `dummy_acc_base` is this line.

TxWitness.vbLhs.why: `lhs[c][0] <== 0` (balance.circom:81) is the base of the input-side chain, folded to a constant: the transparent bucket contributes nothing to the input side. It is the initial value of `PerAssetValueBalanceSat.lhs_chain`. If this signal reappears, something is being added to the inputs, which is what the removed public-input term used to do.

TxWitness.vbRhs.why: The accumulator chains carry N_IN+1 and N_OUT+1 entries, and the top of the rhs chain is gone because `lhs[c][N_IN] === rhs[c][N_OUT]` (balance.circom:99) merges it with the top of the lhs chain. That equality is `PerAssetValueBalanceSat.balanced`, the constraint the whole conservation result rests on; if this signal reappears, the two sides are no longer equated.

TxWitness.dgBlock.why: `out <== h[BLOCKS - 1].out`, `digest <== dg.out` (poly_eval.circom:85, 169) and `digest <== pe.digest` (transact.circom:174) merge the last block's output with the public output `main.digest`. The first three blocks survive. `CoeffDigestSat.out_def` is that merge; if this signal reappears, the public digest is no longer the fold of the coefficients.

SpentSlot.mpChain.why: `cur[0] <== leaf` aliases the note commitment, which is the leaf, and the top `cur[DEPTH]` aliases `mp.mr.root`. Both ends of the chain are merged; the interior levels survive.

BatchSignals.zIsZero.why: `z_nz.out === 0` (poly_eval.circom:37) pins it, as in the transact circuit. That constraint is `PolyEvalSat.z_nonzero`, reached here through `BatchSat.compress`.

BatchSignals.dgBlock.why: `out <== h[BLOCKS - 1].out`, `digest <== dg.out` (poly_eval.circom:85, 242) and `digest <== pe.digest` (tree_update_batch.circom:212) merge the ninth block's output with the public output `main.digest`. The first eight blocks survive. `CoeffDigestSat.out_def`, reached through `BatchSat.digest_def`, is that merge; if this signal reappears, the public digest is no longer the fold of the 36 coefficients.

BatchAppendSignals.oldNode.why: `old_node[0] <== 0` pins the base of the old-root path to a constant, and `old_node[DEPTH]` folds into `old_root` through `old_root === append.old_root`. `old_node[1..DEPTH-1]` survive.

BatchAppendSignals.oldRoot.why: `old_root === append.old_root` merges the gadget's old root with the public input.

BatchAppendSignals.newRoot.why: `new_root === append.new_root` merges the gadget's new root, and with it the last window node `node[29]`, with the public input. The `BATCH_NODES` bound of 29 pins that fold.
